chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Fuḍayl ibn Saʿdān [Saʿdān, variant] from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
There was, in the hilt of the sword of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, a scroll in which was written:
The curse of Allah, the angels, and all people

be upon the one who kills someone other than his killer, or strikes someone other than the one who struck him, or commits an offense, or shelters an offender. And disavowal of one’s lineage, even if slight, is kufr in Allah, the Magnificent.

key_terms.آوَى مُحْدِثاً: gave shelter or protection to an offender
key_terms.أَحْدَثَ حَدَثاً: committed an offense or introduced a punishable violation
key_terms.الِانْتِفَاءُ مِنْ حَسَبٍ: disavowing or denying one’s lineage or family ancestry
key_terms.ذُؤَابَةِ سَيْفِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the hilt or upper fastening of the Messenger of Allah’s sword, where the written scroll was kept
key_terms.كُفْرٌ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ: an act described as disbelief in Allah, the Magnificent
key_terms.لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ: Allah’s curse; expulsion from divine mercy

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about unlawful retaliation, sheltering offenders, and denying one’s lineage?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written statement preserved with the sword of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم condemning unlawful retaliation, protection of offenders, and denial of lineage. It emphasizes the gravity of violating justice in bloodshed and social identity, presenting such acts as deserving divine curse and severe religious condemnation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5174 - Ali ibn Al-Hakam narrated from Al-Fudayl ibn Sadan from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), who said:
"There was a scroll in the hilt of the sword of the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family), and it was written in it:
'The curse of Allah (swt), the angels, and all people

be upon the one who kills someone other than his killer, strikes someone other than the one who struck him, commits an offense, or shelters an offender.
And to disassociate from one's lineage, no matter how small, is an act of disbelief in Allah (swt), the Almighty.'"
